hero.paragraph: Black Elite Transfers moves you across Switzerland and into the Alps in a Mercedes-Benz or Tesla, driven by a chauffeur who knows the roads, the weather and the shortcuts.

homeIntro.heading: A chauffeur service built around one promise
homeIntro.paragraph1: We are a Geneva-based private chauffeur company serving Switzerland, the French and Italian Alps and southern Germany. Every journey is quoted in advance, confirmed by a human, and driven by someone who treats your schedule as their own.
homeIntro.paragraph2: No app queues, no surge pricing, no wondering whether the car will show up. You book, we confirm within thirty minutes, and we are waiting when you arrive.

airport.title: From the gate to the car, without a pause
airport.intro: Your driver is already watching your flight before you land. Whatever the delay, whatever the terminal, the car is there.
airport.bodyHeading: A transfer that absorbs the chaos of travel
paragraphs: Airports are where journeys go wrong — a delayed inbound, a missed connection, an hour lost at baggage reclaim. We plan around all of it. Your flight number is logged at booking, and our dispatch watches it in real time. If you land ninety minutes late, the pickup simply moves with you at no extra cost.

For arrivals, your chauffeur meets you inside the terminal with a name board, helps with luggage and walks you to the car. For departures, we build in the buffer that the route and the season actually need — not the optimistic one a navigation app suggests.

We cover Geneva and Zurich most often, but also Basel, Bern, Lugano, Lyon-Saint-Exupéry, Milan Malpensa and Munich. Private aviation terminals at Geneva and Sion are handled the same way, with airside coordination where the operator allows it.

faq.q: What happens if my flight is delayed?
faq.a: Nothing changes for you. We track the flight and adjust the pickup automatically. Delays are never charged as waiting time.

faq.q: Where exactly will the driver meet me?
faq.a: Inside the arrivals hall, past customs, holding a board with your name. If you prefer a kerbside pickup instead, tell us when booking.

faq.q: Can you carry skis, golf clubs or oversized luggage?
faq.a: Yes — tell us at booking and we will assign the V-Class, which takes skis and large cases comfortably.
Yes, for all ages, free of charge. Please give us the children's ages when you book so we fit the right seat.

ski.title: Mountain roads, handled properly
ski.intro: Winter tyres, chains on board and a driver who has taken these passes in a blizzard. You watch the scenery; we handle the rest.
ski.bodyHeading: The stretch between the airport and the chalet
paragraphs: The transfer to a ski resort is the part of the trip most people underestimate. Snow closes passes, traffic backs up on Saturday changeover days, and the last fifteen minutes up to a chalet can be steeper than anything the route planner suggested. Our drivers do these roads all winter and plan for the conditions rather than the timetable.

Every vehicle runs proper winter tyres from November to April and carries chains. We check pass and road status the morning of your transfer, and if the Grand-Saint-Bernard or the Forclaz is closed we reroute before you notice there was a problem.

Most of our winter work runs from Geneva to Verbier, Zermatt, Courchevel, Val d'Isère, Chamonix and Megève, but we serve any resort in the Valais, Vaud, Savoie and Aosta regions. Group transfers in the V-Class take seven passengers with skis and boards.

faq.q: Can you drive all the way to Zermatt?
faq.a: Zermatt is car-free, so we drive to the Täsch terminal and help you onto the shuttle train with your luggage. It is a twelve-minute ride from there.

faq.q: What if a mountain pass is closed?
faq.a: We check road status the morning of travel and reroute in advance. The quoted price does not change because of a detour.

faq.q: Is there space for skis and boards?
faq.a: Yes. The V-Class carries seven passengers with full ski equipment. Tell us your group size and gear at booking.

faq.q: Do you do Saturday changeover days?
faq.a: Yes, and we plan for them. Saturdays in January and February are the busiest of the season, so we build extra time into the schedule.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a ski transfer?
faq.a: For February half-term and the Christmas and New Year weeks, as early as you can. Outside those peaks, a few days is usually enough.

business.title: A car that waits, so you never do
business.intro: Half-day hire, multi-stop roadshows and client collection, driven with the discretion your meetings require.
business.bodyHeading: Built around a working day, not a single trip
paragraphs: Business travel rarely fits into one A-to-B journey. A morning at the bank in Geneva, lunch in Lausanne, an afternoon client in Nyon and a flight out at seven. We price that as a half-day or full-day hire, with the same car and the same driver from first pickup to last drop-off.

Your chauffeur waits between stops, keeps the cabin at the temperature you asked for, and does not make conversation unless you start it. Calls taken in the back of our cars stay in the back of our cars — every driver works under a confidentiality agreement.

We handle client and delegation collection too, which is often where a company is judged first. Your visitor is met by name, driven in a clean Mercedes-Benz, and delivered to your office without ever having to think about the logistics.

faq.q: How does half-day or full-day hire work?
faq.a: A half-day is four hours and a full day is eight, counted from your first pickup. The car and driver stay with you throughout, including waiting between stops.

faq.q: Can the itinerary change during the day?
faq.a: Yes. Extra stops and timing changes are accommodated where the schedule allows. Anything beyond the booked hours is charged at the agreed hourly rate.

faq.q: Can you collect our clients and visitors?
faq.a: Yes, and it is one of our most requested services. We meet them by name, handle the luggage and deliver them to your address.

about.title: A small company that answers the phone
about.intro: Black Elite Transfers is a Geneva-based private chauffeur service built on the idea that reliability is the only luxury that actually matters.
storyParagraphs: We started Black Elite Transfers after too many journeys that went wrong in the same predictable ways — a driver who did not show, a price that doubled on a rainy evening, a car that arrived with someone else's coffee cup in the door.

So we built the opposite. Prices are fixed at booking and never move. Every request is confirmed by a person, usually within half an hour. The same car and driver stay with you for the whole assignment, and the interior is reset between every single journey.

We are a small team and we intend to stay one. As we take on more clients we bring on drivers we know personally and train them ourselves, because the difference between a good transfer and a bad one is almost always the person behind the wheel.
